content: Ghost of Tsushima (GDC 2021) is the reference for wind coherence: grass, trees, cloth, leaves, smoke, and particles all sample ONE shared wind simulation (direction + gust field), which is what sells 'real wind' - most games fake wind per-system and it reads as incoherent. They add higher-frequency detail via 'vorticles' (invisible wind-generator particles) and local disturbance inputs like character footfalls layered on top of the global field. Key takeaway for small games: a single global wind vector + shared time/phase uniform with a slow gust envelope, plus per-system local detail noise, achieves most of the effect. Sources: GDC Vault 1027124 & 1027033, gamedeveloper.com vorticles article.
